title: The 8253 and 8254 interval timer, its registers
covers: The registers of the 8253 and 8254 interval timer: the three counters and the control word

rows.text: Address lines A1 A0 = 0 0, 0 1 and 1 0 select counter 0, 1 and 2.
The three counters are identical in operation and fully independent, and each may operate in a different mode.
The counting element CE is a 16-bit presettable synchronous down counter that is never read or written directly.
A read returns the output latch OL, which follows CE until a counter latch command freezes it.
A written count is stored in the count register CR.
CRM and CRL are cleared when the counter is programmed, so a one-byte count leaves the other byte zero.
The control word register is not part of a counter, but its contents determine how the counter operates.
Initial counts are written into the counters, not into the control word register, in the format the control word chose.
Write the control word before the initial count and follow the count format it chose; any sequence obeying both is acceptable.
A new initial count may be written at any time without changing the programmed mode, and must follow the programmed format.
With two-byte counts, control must not pass between the two bytes to a routine that writes the same counter.
A simple read returns the count of the selected counter.
The count is read in the programmed format, two bytes for a two-byte count, which need not be read one right after the other.
Reads and writes of one counter may be interleaved: read LSB, write new LSB, read MSB, write new MSB is valid.
With two-byte counts, control must not pass between the two reads to a routine that reads the same counter.
With CS low, RD high, WR low and A1 A0 = 00 the CPU writes into counter 0.
With CS low, RD high, WR low and A1 A0 = 01 the CPU writes into counter 1.
With CS low, RD high, WR low and A1 A0 = 10 the CPU writes into counter 2.
With CS low, RD low, WR high and A1 A0 = 00, 01 or 10 the CPU reads counter 0, 1 or 2.
With count and status latched, the first read of the counter returns status, then one or two reads return the count.
Reading the count in the middle of a two-byte write returns the complement of the byte written first.
A count written between clock edges moves the last update forward by one clock period.
A count written to the speaker counter goes to the speaker emulation with the mode; counter 0 logs its rate when the count changed and the mode is not 0.
A count of 0 is 0x10000 binary or 10000 BCD, and a count of 1 in mode 2 or 3 is 0x10001 or 10001.
On the IBM PC DOSBox-X installs write handlers for ports 0x40, 0x42 and 0x43 and none for 0x41.
In mode 3 a read of the count returns the value with bit 0 cleared, except on the FE2010 type.
A one-byte count write simulates the clock when a clock frequency is set, and in mode 0 sets the output low.
After the first byte of a two-byte count, in mode 0 or 4, counter 0 drops its pending event and sets IRQ 0 from its output.
The count in CR is later transferred to CE, both bytes together, while the control logic loads one register at a time.
For a simple read the CLK input of the selected counter must be inhibited by GATE or external logic, or the count may change and the result is undefined.
TIMER_BIOS_INIT_Configure gives counter 0 the count 0x10000 and a read latch of 0.

rows.text: Address lines A1 A0 = 1 1 select the control word register.
A write with A1 A0 = 11 stores the data in the control word register, where it is read as a control word.
The control word register can only be written to.
Status information is available with the read-back command.
Counters are programmed by a control word, which names the counter it programs, and then an initial count.
A control word is SC1 SC0 RW1 RW0 M2 M1 M0 BCD, written with A1 A0 = 11, CS low, RD high and WR low.
SC selects the counter: 00 counter 0, 01 counter 1, 10 counter 2.
SC = 11 is the read-back command.
RW selects the access format: 01 LSB only, 10 MSB only, 11 LSB first and then MSB.
M selects mode 0 to 5 (M2 is a don't care in modes 2 and 3); 0 is mode 0 and 1 is mode 1.
BCD 0 selects a binary 16-bit counter and 1 a binary coded decimal counter of four decades.
Don't care bits should be 0 to insure compatibility with future Intel products.
The datasheet shows four programming sequences that give each counter its control word, then its LSB and MSB, in different orders; they are only four of many possible.
RW = 00 is the counter latch command, written to the control word register like a control word.
A counter latch command is SC1 SC0 0 0 X X X X: SC1 SC0 pick counter 0, 1 or 2.
Don't care bits in a counter latch command should be 0 for compatibility with future Intel products.
A counter latch command holds the count in the output latch until the CPU reads it or the counter is reprogrammed.
Several counters can be latched; each holds its count until read, and a latch command never changes the programmed mode.
A second latch command on a latched counter is ignored: the count read is the one at the first command.
The read-back command checks the count, mode and OUT and null count states of selected counters; D3 D2 D1 select them.
Read-back is 1 1 COUNT STATUS CNT2 CNT1 CNT0 0: COUNT 0 latches the count, STATUS 0 latches the status, D0 must be 0.
COUNT = 0 latches the count of every selected counter like several latch commands; repeats before a read are ignored.
STATUS = 0 latches the status of the selected counters.
Status must be latched to be read, and a counter's status is read from that counter.
The status byte holds OUT in bit 7, null count in bit 6 and the mode word as last written in bits 5-0.
Null count says whether the last count written to CR has been loaded into CE.
A control word or count write sets null count (second byte if two bytes) and loading CR into CE clears it; only that counter.
Repeated status latches without a read are ignored: the status read is the one at the first command.
Count and status can be latched together with COUNT and STATUS both 0; repeats before the reads are ignored.
With CS low, RD high, WR low and A1 A0 = 11 the CPU writes a control word.
A read with A1 A0 = 11 does nothing: the data bus stays in three-state.
With CS high, or RD and WR both high, nothing happens.
Read-back 11000010 latches count and status of counter 0; 11101100 asks for the status of counters 2 and 1 and latches it for counter 2 only.
A control word write leaves a latched count held: its branch sets control, null count, byte flip-flops and phase, and never touches the latch.
A control word write sets null count to 1; load_count, which a count write calls, does not set it.
A read at offset 3 returns 0 instead of leaving the data bus three-state.
On the 8253 type the read-back command body is empty, and a Todo comment says what the hardware does there is unknown.
A control word write leaves a latched count held, as some DOS games rely on latching a counter; a completed count write releases it.
A second latch command latches the count again, replacing the first one.
Only the lowest counter selected has its status latched.
The status byte's null count bit is the new_mode flag, which write_latch clears when a count is written.
The control word sets new_mode, and a completed count write clears it.
A BCD control word clamps a larger counter to 9999.
A control word write clears a pending status latch of that counter.
A control word for the speaker counter tells the speaker emulation.
Latching counter 0 also raises or lowers IRQ 0 from its output.
A read-back count command is ignored when the counter is halfway through a two-byte read.
A control word write clears both byte flip-flops.
A read-back with COUNT 0 latches each selected counter again, replacing a count latched before.
A read-back with COUNT 0 latches the selected counts again even when one is already latched.
Read-back 11101100 latches the status of counter 1 only, because only the lowest selected counter has its status latched.
A mode of 6 or 7 written is stored as 2 or 3, so the status byte reports that mode, not the one written.
With the option set, a read of any counter returns that counter's own freshly latched status, even though the latch command was for another counter.
A control word write clears update_count and counting of that counter; the code says counting stops until a count is written.
A control word for counter 0 removes its pending event and sets IRQ 0 from the counter output.
The output level of the status byte comes from counter_output, which reads the counter again and returns the stored output.
Until the count is loaded into CE it cannot be read, so a count read or latched before then does not reflect the new count.
DOSBox-X installs read handlers for ports 0x40 to 0x42 only, so port 0x43 has no read handler.
DOSBox-X installs read handlers for ports 0x40 to 0x42 only, so a read of port 0x43 reaches no handler.
TIMER_BIOS_INIT_Configure sets the output of each of the three counters high.
